elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates..." — an express defence duty running to Sparkling and its affiliates, which the original Section 13 lacked (it said only "indemnify ... and hold it harmless").

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of..." with beneficiaries "Sparkling and its affiliates". "Losses" is the defined term from the retained paragraph, so no dangling reference.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Work or the Maintenance Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — covers both the delivered Work and the services, on an allegation (not adjudication) trigger, unlike the retained "is held to constitute an infringement" remedy clause.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling's data caused by Garman".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling shall notify Garman in writing of any such claim" — notice mechanic tied to the new indemnity; the retained ten-day notice continues to apply only to the title-warranty indemnity, so no contradiction.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Garman shall have control of the defence and settlement of the claim" — control is expressly allocated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation in that defence".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's indemnification obligations under this Agreement, if any, are limited to claims arising from content provided by Sparkling and Sparkling's breach of applicable law" — matches both permitted heads and caps any Customer-side indemnity document-wide.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (i) of the inserted paragraph gives a third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in favour of Sparkling.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the condition does not apply because no modification exclusion was added and none is required — the absence of the exclusion is more favourable to Customer than the fallback allows.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is present, which is a Customer-favourable outcome and therefore does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications exclusion is present, again more favourable to Customer than the fallback contemplates.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Retained (a)-(c): Garman shall "procure the right to use the infringing element of the Work", procure an equivalent element, or "replace or modify the element ... so that the infringing portion is no longer infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: The retained (a)-(c) list contains no refund backstop and the insertion adds none; there is no operative language obliging Garman to refund fees if procure/modify/replace is unavailable. Only relevant if the fallback level were the target.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap appears; Section 15 instead disapplies the liability limitation to Section 13 breaches, leaving the indemnity uncapped — a better-than-fallback outcome for Customer, but the literal element is absent.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check confirmed: neither the retained text nor the inserted paragraph contains any multiple-of-fees cap on indemnity liability.

reasons: All ten preferred elements are delivered in a single inserted paragraph: express defend/indemnify/hold-harmless duty to Sparkling and its affiliates, third-party claim trigger, the four required heads (IP allegation as to the Work and Maintenance Services, breach of law, Garman-caused unauthorized access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and notice/control/cooperation mechanics, plus the narrowing of any Sparkling indemnity to Sparkling-provided content and Sparkling's breach of law. The preferred level is therefore position-complete.

The fallback level is not complete (no refund backstop where procure/modify/replace fails, and no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because completion at either level suffices and the preferred level is met. The missing super-cap is Customer-favourable and should not be added.

Minimality holds: the edit is a pure insertion after the existing Section 13 remedies with no deletion or paraphrase of retained language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or extra damages categories, and it reuses the already-defined term "Losses" rather than importing a new damages formula. The retained ten-day notice and (a)-(c) injunction remedies are favourable existing language and are preserved.

Intent is preserved: the new notice mechanic is scoped to "any such claim" under the new paragraph and does not contradict the retained ten-day notice for title-warranty claims; Section 15's carve-out for Section 13 continues to operate on the enlarged indemnity without creating a dangling reference or contradictory retained sentence.

Drafting note only (not a defect): control of "the defence and settlement" is given to Garman without a consent qualifier for settlements imposing non-monetary obligations on Sparkling — the checklist only requires that control be allocated, so this does not affect completeness, but we would ordinarily add "provided that no settlement imposing liability or admission on Sparkling shall be made without Sparkling's consent" if a further round is available.
